title: Restate sharp numerical-range constants (GMRES 2, Arnoldi f(A)b 4, block/matrix-polynomial GMRES 2) in docs, notes and teaching material
summary: The complete Crouzeix theorem (all dimensions, matrix coefficients, Lean-formalized) gives constant 2 for every numerical-range bound. Scalar uses were already covered by human proofs (Lorist-Schwenninger, Jin, Aug 2026); the matrix-coefficient (block GMRES min over matrix polynomials) form is unique to the drop. No software constant depends on it, so the change is to docs only, e.g. the Chebfun Crouzeix example still says 'open, 11.08'.

targets.name: chebfun fov.m (tool used to evaluate FOV bounds)
Embree, How descriptive are GMRES convergence bounds? (uses 1+sqrt2)

beneficiaries: Numerical linear algebra theorists, textbook and survey authors, Chebfun example readers
first_step: Open a PR on chebfun/examples updating Crouzeix.m to: proved (Jin; Lorist-Schwenninger 2026); complete version (OpenAI 2026); constant 2 sharp.
measurement: PR merged; constants updated in the next survey or textbook revision; citation count of the note
risks: Priority disputes with the human scalar proofs. The gain is about 1% of the iterations a bound predicts (0.188/|log rho|). Badea-O'Loughlin-Virtanen 2609.03637 may also imply complete bounds (unchecked).

title: Sharp constant 4 for bivariate matrix functions f{A,B} and Frechet-derivative bounds (Crouzeix-Kressner 5.83 -> 4)
summary: The Crouzeix-Kressner bound ||f{A,B}|| <= K^2 max_{W(A)xW(B)}|f| needs the complete constant for one variable. With the drop it becomes 4, which the nilpotent A=B=J, f=xy example shows is sharp (ratio 4.0000 in my check). Using only the human scalar results gives 2(1+sqrt2)=4.83. For f=exp the classical log-norm bound with constant 1 is already better, so the benefit lies with non-exponential functions (log, fractional powers, Sylvester-type operators).

targets.name: scipy expm_cond (exact Kronecker form; unaffected, shown for contrast)

beneficiaries: Matrix-function conditioning theory, bivariate Krylov analyses
first_step: Send a 2-page note to Kressner and Crouzeix stating the sharp bivariate constant 4 and the open Frechet-specific constant, which lies in [sqrt2, 4] per my search.
measurement: Acknowledged in follow-up papers; Frechet-only sharp constant resolved
risks: Small audience. For expm the log-norm bound already dominates, so the gain is narrower than it looks.

title: Per-matrix certified spectral constant kappa(A,Omega) <= 2 via the structural LMI
summary: Thm. thm:structural makes the optimal similarity the solution of a small LMI, giving a matrix-specific constant often well below 2 (1.08-1.77 for shift matrices in my SDP runs). It costs an n-by-n SDP, far more than the solve it would certify, so it only suits analysis studies with n up to about 100.
first_step: Compare kappa(A,Omega) with Crouzeix ratios on Chebfun gallery matrices (n<=100) where Omega is a disk or ellipse.
measurement: How often kappa is much smaller than 2, and the resulting tightening of FOV bounds
risks: O(n^6) SDP cost; conformal maps are only easy for disks and ellipses.

title: Upstream numerical range / spectral-set library to Mathlib
summary: Mathlib has no numerical-range development. The drop ships about 14k lines of sorry-free Lean (OAI/Analysis/NumericalRange, DirectCrouzeix, HilbertCrouzeix) on Lean v4.34.1, including Toeplitz-Hausdorff and the complete Crouzeix inequality.
beneficiaries: Formalization community; future certified numerical-analysis proofs
first_step: Extract the numerical-range definition and Toeplitz-Hausdorff convexity as the first Mathlib PR.
risks: The code was machine-generated and may need heavy refactoring to meet Mathlib style.

title: Change Krylov / expm / funm software constants or stopping rules based on Crouzeix 2
summary: None of the codes inspected reads a numerical-range constant. SciPy expm_multiply uses the Al-Mohy-Higham theta table with tol=2^-53. Krylov.jl block-GMRES, KrylovKit, ExponentialUtilities and funm_quad all stop on a-posteriori residuals or estimates. FOV bounds over-predict by orders of magnitude in practice (193 actual iterations vs about 1.56e5 predicted on a convection-diffusion test), so the 17% constant change has no effect on software.
risks: Over-selling the result as a numerics speedup.

title: Certify the sharp worst-case W2^{1/3} exponent for semi-discrete / LOT map estimators with a uniform convex reference
summary: With a uniform convex source, ||T_mu - T_nu||_{L2} <= C* W2^{1/3} uniformly over compactly supported targets, and 1/3 is sharp even for three atoms. Plug-in estimators T_{nu_n} then have worst-case rate n^{-1/12} for d<4 and n^{-1/(3d)} for d>4 with no target regularity. That improves the W1^{1/6} rates for d>=3, ties the W1^{1/4} route at d=3, beats it for d>=4 and loses to it at d=2. LOT embeddings get the sandwich W2 <= ||T_mu-T_nu|| <= C* W2^{1/3}, and the uniform square-root conjecture is dead.
beneficiaries: OT-statistics theorists, LOT users needing worst-case distortion statements
first_step: Add a Notes paragraph to the POT semidiscrete docstring, and write a short survey note comparing the W2^{1/3}, W1^{1/4} and W1^{1/6} routes.
measurement: Doc PR merged; exponent cited in the next OT-statistics survey
risks: Practitioners never consult worst-case exponents. PyTransKit LOT uses a discrete reference, so the theorem does not apply to it.

title: A-posteriori map-error certificates in semi-discrete solvers from the explicit C*
summary: C* = sqrt(12 d R^2 (1+sqrt162)^2 + 28 L^2 P_K/|K|) is 67.7 on the unit square and 239 at d=10. The certificate beats the trivial diameter bound only when W2 < ~1e-5, i.e. a marginal TV of about 1e-11. A 10%-of-diameter guarantee needs W2 <= 9e-9, about 1e16 samples in d=2. Vacuous.
risks: Shipping vacuous bounds that mislead users.

title: Sharpen the constant in one-third Brenier stability (C0=162 vs extremal ~0.63)
summary: The extremal three-atom family has ratio ||dT||/W2^{1/3} = 0.630 on [-1,1]^2, while the proven C* is 95.4, a gap of about 150x. Closing it would help theory, but the 1/6 power in any marginal-residual certificate keeps practical certificates weak.
first_step: Numerically estimate the sup of ||dT||/W2^{1/3} over random small-atom targets on the square, using pysdot.
measurement: Ratio of the empirical sup to C*
risks: Even an optimal constant leaves certificates weak because of the 1/3 exponent.

title: Sharp vector log-concave entropy-gap corollaries: capacity and MSE rate-distortion gap <= 0.6044 bits/dim (any log-concave vector)
summary: h(f) >= m + 1/2 log det Cov gives D(f||Gaussian with same Cov) <= m(1/2 log(2 pi e) - 1) = 0.418939 nats = 0.604401 bits per dimension, sharp and with no symmetry assumption. This replaces Marsiglietti-Kostina's symmetric-only vector constants, which grow with n (2.24 bits/dim at n=2, 7.2 at n=1000). The scalar case and its capacity corollary are already in Melbourne-Nayar-Roberto (2023/2026). Exponential noise with Gaussian input reaches 0.6044 bits at P>=100, so the bound is tight.
beneficiaries: Information theorists (non-Gaussian channel and source bounds)
first_step: Write a 1-page note with the vector capacity and SLB-gap corollaries, crediting MNR for the scalar case.
measurement: Note posted and cited; constants adopted in the next survey
risks: Not formalized (the scalar rational certificate passes; I ran it). The gain is low-stakes: real systems compute D(Z||G) for the known noise law directly.

title: Claim the 1.05 -> 0.604 bit improvement as new
summary: The scalar log-concave bound h >= 1 + 1/2 log Var and its capacity corollary (gap 1/2 log(2 pi/e) ~ 0.42 nats) were published by Melbourne-Nayar-Roberto. Only the vector extension is new.

title: Dimension-free LSI corollaries for sampler mixing on psi2 log-concave targets (In-and-Out, ULA)
summary: C_LSI <= C a^2 for centered log-concave laws with a-subgaussian linear marginals. Fed into In-and-Out (Kook-Vempala-Zhang, Cor 6), it gives cold-start complexity Õ(d^2 C a^2) instead of Õ(d^{2.5}) from C_LSI <~ D. Fed into ULA/LMC in KL (Vempala-Wibisono), it gives a dimension-free LSI constant. C is non-explicit (proof by contradiction), so these are complexity statements only, not certified step counts.
first_step: Write the cold-start In-and-Out and LMC-in-KL corollaries, and list natural psi2 bodies (l_p balls with p>=2, products) where this beats tensorization or Bakry-Emery.
measurement: A corollary note; whether any practically relevant target class is uniformly psi2 after rounding
risks: Non-explicit C; unverified, unformalized 50-page proof; many practical targets (polytopes, logistic posteriors) are only psi1.

title: Retune sampler step sizes or iteration budgets (volesti, Stan, BlackJAX) from the subgaussian LSI
summary: C is not explicit and the subgaussian parameter a is unknown for real targets. Production samplers adapt step size from acceptance rates and ESS, so no code change follows.

title: Memory-sample lower bound for noiseless Gaussian regression as a design rule for streaming least squares
summary: With o(d^2) or A*d^2 bits, Omega(d log 1/eps) noiseless samples are needed, with explicit constant 2^-16 in the o(d^2) case (Lean-formalized). This matches Kaczmarz/SGD (~1.39 d log2 1/eps) up to a factor of about 9e4. It confirms the folklore that sub-quadratic-memory streaming solvers cannot beat O(d log 1/eps) samples. No practitioner decision changes.
risks: Noiseless isotropic Gaussian rows and fixed A only.

title: Courtade-Kumar / Hellinger inequalities as engineering guidance for one-bit summaries
summary: Proves that no Boolean function of uniform bits keeps more mutual information about a BSC-noisy copy than a dictator. A human computer-assisted, Lean-verified proof (Chen-Gohari-Javanmard-Lin-Mirrokni-Nair-Woodruff, arXiv 2609.24931, Sept 21) predates the drop paper (Sept 24). This confirms practice (forward a raw bit); nothing to implement.
risks: Stylized model (uniform inputs, BSC, one output bit).

title: Exact KS thresholds at all degrees: 3-community SBM (a-b)^2 > 3(a+2b), and Jukes-Cantor ancestral-reconstruction transition at p* = (3/4)(1 - d^{-1/2})
summary: The ferromagnetic four-state channel is exactly JC69 with lambda = exp(-4t/3). Non-reconstruction at d*lambda^2 <= 1 makes the deep-tree root unrecoverable iff p >= (3/4)(1-d^{-1/2}): p* = 0.2197 and t* = (3/8)ln2 = 0.260 subs/site for binary trees. Combined with Roch (O(log n) sites below KS) and Mossel-Roch-Sly (poly(n) above g_ML), this pins the JC sequence-length phase transition at KS on regular trees. The SBM corollary removes the large-degree restriction of Mossel-Sly-Sohn 2025. The hard direction relies on exact-arithmetic C++ certificates (not in Lean); the four-state rational checks pass but the full certificate needs Boost.
beneficiaries: Phylogenetics theory (Steel's conjecture under JC), SBM benchmark authors
first_step: Write the JC sequence-length corollary, checking whether MRS's g_ML is defined on the same regular-tree family. Re-run the full C++ certificates on a machine with Boost.
risks: Equal branch lengths and regular or Poisson trees only. The computer-assisted direction is unformalized. Practitioners (IQ-TREE/RAxML ASR) do not operate in this idealized regime.

title: Perceptron free energies and jamming exponents applied to ML or packing practice
summary: These are variational formulas for random-label storage at positive temperature with bounded soft potentials, plus certified jamming exponents gamma ~ 0.412693 and theta ~ 0.423108 that match the Charbonneau-Kurchan-Parisi-Urbani-Zamponi predictions. Capacity, teacher-student and generalization settings are excluded. This rigorously confirms physics predictions; no practice changes.
